correctness.rationale: For the spherical orthant the centroid is exactly the all-ones direction by symmetry. In dimension three every admissible normal is, up to permutation and sign, (a,1-a,-1), 0<=a<=1. The complementary cut is an explicitly parameterized spherical triangle. Factoring its solid-angle denominator yields the claimed closed form; an independently derived spherical-coordinate integral has strictly negative second derivative and symmetry about a=1/2, proving the unique extremal orbits. In all dimensions absolute standard Gaussians induce Haar directions on the orthant; conditioning on a half-normal gives the expectation identity; strict concavity plus the leave-one-out Jensen argument proves strict dimensional monotonicity; the strong law and bounded convergence give the error-function limit. Tested the independent integral and Gaussian Monte Carlo using the packaged verify.py; finite checks are not substitutes for these proofs.

originality.rationale: Actual targeted indexed-record, historical-claim, and published-primary comparisons found no theorem implying the exact full octant cut spectrum and its unique optimizer, paired with the higher-dimensional one-versus-rest monotonic sequence. The motivating universal spherical Grünbaum bound is weaker, and the older Winternitz-type theorem reduces arbitrary disks to unspecified triangles rather than solving the chosen all-right one. The basic solid-angle formula and concave sample-mean order are classical ingredients, not independently claimed new. Unindexed earlier computations remain a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The spherical positive orthant is a canonical nondegenerate spherical simplex, so its minimum centroidal hemisphere fraction is a natural exact body invariant and direct benchmark for the new spherical Grünbaum inequality. The result gives a complete all-normal, sharp, equality-classified spectrum rather than evaluating a chosen cut; its fixed-domain constant is strictly above the universal 4/9. The same extremal orbit extends as a natural one-versus-rest cut across all dimensions with a strict monotonic law and exact limiting Gaussian constant, documenting persistent anisotropy. No general universal improvement or higher-dimensional global optimizer is claimed.
